input.problem: Language models trained for knowledge-graph reasoning are typically supervised on isolated head-relation-tail triples (or single paths), which removes the surrounding passage/graph context needed for multi-step inference. Two consequences are claimed: (a) models fail to learn the contextual cues that support multi-hop composition, and (b) noisy or incomplete base facts cause 'one-hop' errors that propagate and cap deeper-hop performance. Existing KGQA work largely injects subgraphs at inference time (retrieval/prompting) rather than changing the training-time supervision signal, and it is unclear whether enriching the supervision with co-passage context improves transfer from shallow to deeper multi-hop queries.
input.target_domain: Multi-hop knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) and knowledge-graph-grounded language-model fine-tuning/reasoning.
input.target_system: An instruction-following / fine-tunable language model (order 1-7B parameters) that is supervised on KG triples or reasoning paths and evaluated on standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks (MetaQA 2-hop/3-hop; WebQuestionsSP; ComplexWebQuestions). PTLM+graph baselines such as EmbedKGQA and GreaseLM/MHGRN are the comparison systems.
input.proposed_method: Three coupled components. (1) Context-enriched supervision: for each target triple or path, retrieve additional triples from the same source passage to form a local context subgraph, and present this subgraph together with the primary supervision signal during fine-tuning. H2 (transfer): RL optimization restricted to lower-hop instances improves accuracy on deeper-hop queries that were never directly trained. H3 (repair): The adaptive one-hop repair loop reduces one-hop failure rate and further improves multi-hop accuracy beyond context enrichment alone.
